# OpenBin.ai — The Open Binary Project

> OpenBin (official name: **The Open Binary Project**, also commonly written as OpenBin or OpenBin.ai) is a free, open-source, collaborative platform for AI-assisted reverse engineering, decompilation, and malware analysis. It pairs traditional analysis tooling (Ghidra, JADX) with an agent layer driven by the user's own LLM credentials — the agent does the grunt work of reading decompiled code, tracing call chains, and drafting reports. It runs in the browser as a hosted web app (app.openbin.ai / openapk.ai); projects live in the cloud, so work is accessible from anywhere and shareable with collaborators. The source is AGPL-3.0 and free for researchers.

OpenBin is a hosted, cloud-based web application, free to use for researchers. (Because the source is AGPL-3.0 on GitHub, it can also be self-hosted, but the primary, recommended way to use it is the hosted app.) The platform is multi-product but shares one core: auth, symbol indexing, the agent layer, the report engine, a collaborative community feed, and BYOK credential storage with KEK-encrypted secrets.

**BYOK economics:** the agent layer supports Anthropic, OpenAI, or AWS Bedrock. Every user brings their own API key, so they pay $0 for AI inference — the platform never centralizes LLM spend. Keys are encrypted at rest, with per-user token budgets and a full audit log of every LLM call.

## What you can analyze

- **Native binaries** — ELF, PE, and Mach-O executables. Ghidra decompiles to pseudo-C, shown side-by-side with disassembly and Ghidra-style cross-highlighting (click a line/variable, see the corresponding machine instructions).
- **Android APKs** — JADX decompilation with IDE-style navigation, native-library (.so) analysis, crypto reconstruction, and network call-site harvesting (via OpenAPK.ai).
- **npm packages** — and loose JavaScript / TypeScript, for supply-chain malware review.
- **PyPI packages** — wheels and sdists, plus loose Python scripts.
- **PowerShell** — .ps1 / .psm1 scripts (static behavior + IOC detection).
- **Shell scripts** — bash, sh, zsh (static behavior + IOC detection).

## Live products

- [OpenBin.ai](https://app.openbin.ai/): native binary reverse engineering — ELF / PE / Mach-O. Ghidra decompile + disassembly, AI hotspots, call chains, string & import analysis, side-by-side cross-highlighting.
- [OpenAPK.ai](https://openapk.ai/): Android APK reverse engineering. JADX decompile, AI static analysis, call-chain tracing with AI-narrated summaries, crypto/obfuscation decoder detection, screenshot capture + annotation, customizable MAR and VRR report templates.

## Key concepts

- **Collaborative**: the headline value prop. Publish a finished analysis as a public report, cite findings from other researchers, and build a shared, queryable corpus of how malware and vulnerabilities actually work.
- **Agent-native**: the UI is built around an LLM agent that reads code the way a researcher would — file-aware, symbol-aware, package-aware — and cites file:line on every answer. Not a chatbot bolted onto a traditional decompiler.
- **BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)**: every user supplies their own Anthropic / OpenAI / AWS Bedrock credentials; $0 inference cost; the platform never centralizes LLM spend.
- **Cloud-based**: hosted web app; projects are accessible from anywhere and shareable. Native-binary decompilation can also be run locally via the OpenBin CLI (Ghidra on your own machine), which then uploads the results.
- **Free & open source**: AGPL-3.0 on GitHub, free for researchers.

## CLI

The OpenBin CLI runs Ghidra/JADX locally for users who'd rather not use cloud compute, then uploads the decompiled result to their account. Install with `curl -fsSL https://openbin.ai/install.sh | sh`; update with `openbin update`.

## Glossary

- **MAR**: Malware Analysis Report — section-templated report optimised for malware triage (sample overview, static findings, IOCs, recommendations, analyst notes).
- **VRR**: Vulnerability Research Report — section-templated report optimised for vuln research (target, attack surface, auth/storage, network, vulnerabilities with CWE + severity, repro, remediation).
- **KEK**: Key Encryption Key — the AES-256 master key used to wrap per-user LLM credentials at rest.
- **JADX**: Java decompiler used to extract Android source from APK / DEX.
- **Ghidra**: NSA-released reverse engineering framework, used to decompile native binaries (ELF/PE/Mach-O) to pseudo-C.
